description: Find files whose name or path matches a glob under a directory. Use when you know a name or path pattern but not the location. Do not use it for file contents; use `search_text` instead. To browse a folder, use `list`. Matches files, never directories. Skips hidden entries, .gitignore matches, and build folders unless includeHidden or includeIgnored. Scanning stops at 10,000 matches (stoppedReason maxResults) or the time limit (FS_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS, default 5 s; stoppedReason timeout) and still returns what it found. path must be an existing directory; a file path is rejected. maxResults sizes a page, not the scan; page on with nextCursor (expires after about 60 s, then search again without it). Returns root, results[{ path }], totalMatches, filesScanned, and when set nextCursor, stoppedReason, skippedInaccessible (entries it could not read), excludedDirs (skipped folders: total and first 5), resourceUri (all kept matches). Paths are relative to root when unambiguous, otherwise absolute.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Pass it unchanged for the next page. Pages come from one snapshot taken on the first call. It expires after ~60s; if rejected, retry without a cursor.

maxDepth.description: Max directory depth. 0 scans only the base directory. Omit for no limit.

maxResults.description: Files per page; totalMatches counts all kept matches.

path.description: Existing directory to search under. Required with several roots. Patterns with / match from here.

pattern.description: Glob. Without / it matches file names at any depth (*.ts). With / it matches paths relative to path (src/**/*.ts).

sortBy.description: name: by file name across folders, ties by path. Sorts the first 10,000 kept matches before paging.

name: find_files
title: Find Files
